title: Richard Sutton – Father of RL thinks LLMs are a dead end
excerpt:
Richard Sutton is the father of reinforcement learning, winner of the 2024 Turing Award, and author of The Bitter Lesson. And he thinks LLMs are a dead end. After interviewing him, my steel man of Richard’s position is this: LLMs aren’t capable of learning on-the-job, so no matter how much we scale, we’ll need *some* new architecture to enable continual learning. And once we have it, we won’t need a special training phase — the agent will just learn on-the-fly, like all humans, and indeed, like all animals. This new paradigm will render our current approach with LLMs obsolete.

In our interview, I did my best to represent the view that LLMs might function as the foundation on which experiential learning can happen… Some sparks flew. A big thanks to the Alberta Machine Intelligence Institute for inviting me up to Edmonton and for letting me use their studio and equipment. Enjoy!

title: The $25 Billion Gamble That Could Change Canada Forever
excerpt:
Canada’s $25 billion Trans Mountain Pipeline isn’t just about oil — it’s about independence.

For decades, nearly 99% of Canadian oil exports flowed south into U.S. pipelines, where Americans controlled prices and profits. This left Canada dependent, vulnerable, and often losing $15–20 billion every year due to the “Canadian discount.”

But after half a century of battles, geography, and politics, Canada finally built its way out of America’s economic grip. The Trans Mountain Expansion opened in 2024, connecting Alberta’s oil sands to Pacific markets and giving Canada direct access to buyers in China, Japan, South Korea, and India.

In this documentary, we’ll explore: Why Canada’s oil wealth was trapped for decades. How American refineries and politics kept control. The brutal challenges of building across the Rockies. Why the $25 billion gamble was worth it. How this single pipeline reshaped Canada’s role in global energy.
This isn’t just about oil. It’s about geography, sovereignty, and the future of nations.
